name: Gmail
_comment: client_id ships empty on purpose: Fused still has to publish a Google Cloud project with a Desktop OAuth client. Google's desktop clients are public clients that must still send their (non-secret, by Google's own docs) client_secret at the token endpoint, so a pack never ships one: FUSED_RENDER_CONNECT_GMAIL_CLIENT_ID and FUSED_RENDER_CONNECT_GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET fill both at load, and Advanced on the card takes the id and secret of your own Desktop client (Google Cloud Console > APIs & Services > Credentials, with the Gmail API enabled). Three Google cards (Gmail, Calendar, Docs) on purpose: each asks for only its own scopes. The same Google client may serve all three. Scopes are gmail.send and gmail.labels only, on purpose: every Gmail scope that reads mail (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.metadata, mail.google.com) is in Google's restricted tier, which costs a paid annual CASA assessment; these two are the sensitive tier (free brand review). So this card sends mail and manages label definitions, and cannot read, search, label or trash messages.
privacy: Sign-in and every call go straight from this computer to Google. The token stays on this computer. Fused runs no server in this flow.
